item.title: DevSweep 0.3.0
item.description:
• First release signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple: DevSweep opens without Gatekeeper warnings.
  • Updating from 0.1.0 or 0.2.0: grant Full Disk Access once more in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Full Disk Access. Later updates keep it.
  • Safe to Clean now finds old Rust incremental build sessions in Cargo target folders.
  • DevSweep skips Cargo profiles that are in the middle of a build, so files being written are never suggested.

item.title: DevSweep 0.2.0
item.description:
This build is ad-hoc signed, not notarized: DevSweep has no Developer ID certificate yet.

  • First install: macOS blocks the app. Open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.
  • After each update: grant Full Disk Access again in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Full Disk Access.

Changes

  • Follow the macOS accent and label colors instead of a fixed violet

item.title: DevSweep 0.1.0
item.description:
This build is ad-hoc signed, not notarized: DevSweep has no Developer ID certificate yet.

  • First install: macOS blocks the app. Open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.
  • After each update: grant Full Disk Access again in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Full Disk Access.

Changes

The first public build of DevSweep, a Mac app with a command-line tool. It measures developer caches and cleans them safely: Xcode DerivedData and archives, simulators and runtimes, package-manager caches, and build output inside your projects.

  • Smart Scan: one button measures everything, with a percent progress bar, the current step, and a Stop button.
  • Safe to Clean: items DevSweep can rebuild or re-download on its own, ranked in tiers from safest to least safe. Each item says what cleaning it costs you.
  • Needs Review: findings that need a decision first, such as stale or orphaned items, duplicates, oversized or growing folders, and anything unclassified.
  • Space: where your disk space goes, group by group.
  • Menu bar only: DevSweep lives in the menu bar and keeps watch in the background. Background checks never clean anything. A Dock icon can be turned on in Settings.
  • Automatic updates: DevSweep checks for updates once a day and installs them when you quit. Updates and the feed are signed (Sparkle).

Install

  • Download DevSweep-0.1.0.dmg below, open it and drag DevSweep to Applications.
  • This build is ad-hoc signed: DevSweep has no Apple Developer ID yet. The first time you open it, macOS blocks it. Go to System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.
  • Grant Full Disk Access in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Full Disk Access, so DevSweep can measure everything. Grant it again after each update, until DevSweep has a Developer ID.

Requires macOS 26 or later.
